seo.title: Best Tools for Bun in 2026
seo.description: Top Bun tools for bundling, testing, deployment, and runtime development. Practical picks from a developer using Bun in production.

introduction: Bun went from hype to genuinely useful fast. I've moved several scripts, APIs, and even a few production services to Bun — the speed gains are real but the ecosystem is still catching up. These tools represent what actually works with Bun today, not what's theoretically compatible.

categories.name: Bundling & Build Tools
categories.description: Plugins, configurations, and tools that extend Bun's built-in bundler and build system.

items.name: Bun Built-in Bundler
items.description: Bun's native bundler is fast and handles most use cases out of the box — JSX, TypeScript, tree-shaking, and code splitting. Still lacks some esbuild plugin compatibility, but it's improving every release.
items.highlight: No extra dependency — bundling is built into the runtime

items.name: bun-plugin-html
items.description: An HTML entry point plugin for Bun's bundler that handles multi-page apps. Processes HTML files, resolves script and link tags, and outputs optimized bundles. Fills a gap the built-in bundler doesn't cover yet.

items.name: bun-plugin-tailwindcss
items.description: Integrates Tailwind CSS processing directly into Bun's bundler pipeline. Eliminates the need for PostCSS in Bun projects. Still community-maintained, so check compatibility with your Tailwind version.

items.name: esbuild
items.description: While Bun has its own bundler, esbuild remains relevant for its massive plugin ecosystem. Many Bun projects still use esbuild for production builds when specific plugins are needed.

items.name: Bun Macros
items.description: A Bun-specific feature that runs code at bundle time and inlines the result. Replace environment checks, configuration loading, and build-time computations with zero runtime cost. Powerful but Bun-only.
items.highlight: Run code at bundle time and inline the result

categories.name: Testing & Quality
categories.description: Tools for testing Bun applications, from the built-in test runner to coverage and assertion libraries.

items.name: Bun Test
items.description: Bun's built-in test runner with Jest-compatible API. Runs tests significantly faster than Jest or Vitest with zero configuration. Snapshot testing, mocking, and lifecycle hooks all included.
items.highlight: Jest-compatible tests at Bun speed — zero config needed

items.name: Playwright
items.description: Works seamlessly with Bun for E2E testing. Run your Bun server in the test setup, then test with Playwright's browser automation. The combination is surprisingly smooth.

items.name: happy-dom
items.description: A fast JavaScript implementation of the browser DOM for server-side testing. Lighter and faster than jsdom, making it ideal for Bun's speed-focused philosophy. Great for component testing without a browser.
items.highlight: 2-3x faster than jsdom for DOM simulation

items.name: Biome
items.description: Bun and Biome share the same philosophy — replace slow JavaScript tools with fast native alternatives. Biome handles linting and formatting for Bun projects without the ESLint config headache.

items.name: c8
items.description: V8's built-in code coverage tool that works with Bun test. Generates coverage reports without instrumenting your code. Lightweight alternative to Istanbul for Bun projects.

items.name: MSW (Mock Service Worker)
items.description: Works with Bun for mocking HTTP requests in tests. The Node.js adapter is compatible with Bun's runtime. Essential for testing API integrations without hitting real endpoints.

categories.name: Runtime & Development
categories.description: Tools that enhance Bun's runtime capabilities, development workflow, and developer experience.

items.name: Hono
items.description: A lightweight web framework that runs on Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, and Node.js. The fastest way to build APIs with Bun — middleware, routing, and validation in under 14KB.
items.highlight: Ultra-fast web framework designed for Bun and edge runtimes

items.name: Elysia
items.description: A Bun-native web framework with end-to-end type safety and a plugin system. Built specifically for Bun's APIs, so it squeezes out performance other frameworks leave on the table. Bun-only though.
items.highlight: Built for Bun from scratch — end-to-end type-safe APIs

items.name: Bun SQLite
items.description: Bun includes a high-performance SQLite driver built in. No npm install, no native addon compilation. Perfect for local-first apps, embedded databases, and prototyping.
items.highlight: Built-in SQLite driver — no dependencies needed

items.name: Bun Shell
items.description: Write shell scripts in JavaScript with Bun's built-in $ template literal. Cross-platform, pipeable, and you get JavaScript's full power. Replaced most of my bash scripts.
items.highlight: Write cross-platform shell scripts in JavaScript

items.name: Bun Workers
items.description: Bun's implementation of Web Workers for multi-threaded JavaScript. Uses message passing and shared memory for CPU-intensive work. The API matches the browser standard, so code is portable.

items.name: dotenvx
items.description: A better dotenv for Bun and Node projects. Supports encryption, multiple environments, and variable expansion. Works seamlessly with Bun's runtime and doesn't require any Bun-specific setup.

categories.name: Deployment & DevOps
categories.description: Tools and platforms for deploying and running Bun applications in production environments.

items.name: Docker (Bun Official Image)
items.description: Bun provides official Docker images based on Debian and Alpine. The images are small and production-ready. The oven/bun image is the easiest way to deploy Bun apps in containerized environments.
items.highlight: Official lightweight Docker images for Bun

items.name: Fly.io
items.description: Deploy Bun apps globally with a Dockerfile and fly launch. Edge deployment with persistent volumes and built-in Postgres. One of the few platforms that runs Bun well without workarounds.
items.highlight: Global edge deployment that works great with Bun

items.name: Railway
items.description: Detects and deploys Bun projects automatically from git. Zero-config deployment with built-in databases and cron jobs. The simplest path from git push to production for Bun apps.

items.name: Render
items.description: Supports Bun as a runtime environment with native build support. Auto-scaling, managed databases, and background workers. Straightforward pricing without the surprises of serverless billing.

items.name: Coolify
items.description: Self-hostable PaaS that runs Bun apps via Docker on your own servers. Full control over infrastructure with a Vercel-like developer experience. No per-deployment or per-request pricing.
items.highlight: Self-hosted deployment platform with no usage fees

items.name: Bun Compile
items.description: Bun's built-in single-executable compiler bundles your app into a standalone binary. No runtime installation needed on the target machine. Perfect for CLI tools and distributing apps.
items.highlight: Compile your app into a single executable binary
